problem.claim: Improve the efficiency of online reinforcement learning updates that reuse stored experience through replay buffers.

gap.claim: Uniform replay wastes updates on less relevant transitions, while prioritizing rare useful samples can promote overfitting.

contributions.claim: A prioritized parametric agent memory that uses generative models to capture online experience, densify past experience, and guide generations toward relevant history.
An implementation using conditional diffusion models and curiosity- or value-based relevance functions.
An account of how guidance promotes diversity in generated transitions and reduces overfitting.

stated_novelty.claim: The work replaces sample-only prioritization with a prioritized, generative, parametric version of agent memory that both densifies and guides replayed experience.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report consistent improvements in performance and sample efficiency across state-based and pixel-based domains.
The authors report that the approach can train policies at higher update-to-data ratios than prior methods.
The authors report that guidance increases diversity in generated transitions and reduces overfitting.

narrative_sequence.summary: Online RL commonly reuses experience through replay buffers for value-function updates.
Uniform replay may be inefficient, but prioritizing useful rare samples can overfit.
The paper proposes prioritized parametric memory with generative experience densification and relevance-guided generation.
The recipe is instantiated with conditional diffusion and curiosity- or value-based relevance metrics.
The authors report gains across state and pixel domains, diversity and overfitting mechanisms, and support for higher update-to-data ratios.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs a relevance-guided generation mechanism with an explicit diversity and overfitting account, rather than describing prioritization only as a performance heuristic.

lessons.interpretation: A method claim becomes more informative when the abstract links the intervention to a proposed mechanism and its tradeoff.
lessons.application: When introducing a selective data-generation method, state both the selection signal and the mechanism by which it is expected to avoid concentration on rare examples.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the work has no supported mechanistic analysis or when selection is not central to the method.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, baselines, numerical effect sizes, statistical uncertainty, or the exact update-to-data ratios.
It does not establish whether the reported improvements hold uniformly across all tested settings or quantify the separate effects of densification and guidance.
